scope: independent actual-H100 GELU recordings, not neural model outputs and not candidate output; tests only
statement: Four synthetic GELU recordings made on a real NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 with torch 2.5.1+cu118. Each case stores the float32 input plus the CUDA torch.nn.functional.gelu outputs for approximate='none', approximate='tanh' and the erf composite 0.5*x*(1+erf(x*sqrt(0.5))). They are the immutable reference for test/proteinmpnn/test_gelu_compat.py and are diagnostic oracles: no product code imports them and no expected value is produced by the code under test. The files are bundled byte-identically in this directory and are read-only test assets.
source_directory: external NVIDIA H100 recording; arrays bundled byte-identically in this directory
copied_by: byte-identical copy of the external H100 recording into the repository test assets
reference_identity: torch.nn.functional.gelu(x, approximate='none') on the H100 (CUDA exact erf kernel); never produced by rfantibody.proteinmpnn.gelu_compat.exact_gelu

array_keys.input: float32 input tensor recorded with the strides listed in manifest.json
array_keys.erf_composite: CUDA 0.5*x*(1+torch.erf(x*sqrt(0.5))), measured bit-identical to gelu_none on every case

recorded_findings.note: These values are re-verified from the recorded arrays by test_gelu_holdout_assets_integrity; they are not re-measured on CUDA.

cases.note: numel 4099 float32 = 16396 bytes, not a multiple of 32; used on the device with an element-offset-1 slice
values drawn from the ProteinMPNN activation range
saturated tails where the tanh approximation is most visible

recorded from a non-contiguous (34, 2)-strided view; the npz itself stores the value array contiguously (numpy cannot preserve a stride), and test_gelu_npu_true_strided_and_unaligned_route reconstructs the recorded stride on the device

tolerances.note: declared in test/proteinmpnn/test_gelu_compat.py before the replay and never relaxed after inspecting results
